svg.aria-label: Where code resumes after await: in a UI app the continuation is posted back to the UI thread's queue; with ConfigureAwait(false) or in ASP.NET Core it runs on any pool thread
svg.text: AFTER await FINISHES, WHO RUNS THE REST OF THE METHOD?

g.text: is free runs the rest of the method.

svg.text: A UI app has a special thread, and only that thread may update the screen. It works through a mailbox.
So by default, await posts "the rest of the method" into that mailbox. That's the SynchronizationContext.
ASP.NET Core has no such context. The rest of the method runs on any free pool thread.

g.text: await x.ConfigureAwait(false) means "don't use the mailbox, any thread will do".
Library code should use it (it might be called from a UI app). In ASP.NET Core app code
it changes nothing, so you can leave it out. It also prevents the deadlock in the next section.
